newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash prices off slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash prices off slightly.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond cash prices were off slightly in early trade, amid deeper declines in municipal futures.
"The market is very much overbought, and probably needs to take a little bit of a rest in here," one trader said, adding that the bid side for cash was off by about one basis point.
"We actually had a decent week this week, we do have several accounts in here buying bonds," he said.
A second trader cited "selective buying going on in bonds," with good call structures in demand.
"They seem to be trading, and the Street still seems to be kind of awash in some of the '03 call bonds and some of the weaker structures," the trader said.
The market appeared to holding up fairly well ahead of the next week's substantial new supply.

"You would think that people would show more respect for it, but what's happened is over the last couple of days is that there's been a couple of different insurance companies who've paid what people feel to be very big prices for bonds," the trader said.
"And I guess the perception is that they will continue to do so, and that the new issue market is quite a good place for people to buy some bonds these days."
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was down 13/32 at 117. The December T-bond contract was down 11/32 at 114-30/32. The MOB spread was 66 ticks.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 14/32 at 100-19/32 to yield 6.45 percent. On the economic front, the Federal Reserve said industrial production fell 0.5 percent in October, down from a revised O.3 percent rise the prior month.
Meanwhile, capacity utilization stood at 82.7 percent for the month, compared to a revised 83.4 in September.

"What we're looking at here is a pullback in manufacturing activity," Moody's Investors Service economist John Lonski said during an interview on Reuters Financial Television. "I'm struck by the across-the-board weakness in this report on industrial production."
